title: Felix and the Cover
premise: Noor Kavanagh, a crash investigator whose wife and daughter died in row twelve of Flight 4471, has spent twelve years in witness protection after testifying about the sabotaged sensor the manufacturer buried. When the safe house appears on a real estate site with interior photos — including one showing his hidden evidence wall — Noor realizes someone inside the program sold him out. Hunted by an assassin named Veyra and betrayed by handlers in three governments who each want the truth silenced for their own reasons, Noor goes off-grid with Mara Ellison, the photographer whose listing exposed him and who becomes both accomplice and love interest. In the end, Noor trades himself to Veyra to get the evidence to a tribunal, survives by turning Veyra against her employers, and finally speaks row twelve's names aloud at the hearing — choosing truth over the invisibility that kept him alive but never let him live.
about_author: Isandro Pemberton is a former aviation insurance adjuster who spent a decade reading crash reports before turning to fiction. He writes from a coastal town he refuses to name, on the theory that everyone deserves one unlisted address.

chapters.title: The Listing
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Scrolling property sites out of boredom, he finds his own safe house for sale — eleven photos, including the hallway where his evidence wall hides behind drywall. The beat is cold dread: twelve years of rules just collapsed.

chapters.title: Row Twelve
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter, Noor's POV. The crash, the identification process, and the testimony that put him into protection. Establishes what was sabotaged and who benefited. Emotional beat: grief fossilized into procedure.

chapters.title: Handler Ghosts
chapters.summary: Noor calls his handler, Aldous Reeve, who insists the listing is a database error and orders him to stay put. Noor notices Reeve's answers are rehearsed. Beat: first crack of doubt in the system that saved him.

chapters.title: The Photographer
chapters.summary: Mara Ellison's POV. She took the listing photos as a routine gig; now men in unmarked cars are asking her about 'the tenant.' She photographs their plates instead of answering. Beat: her instinct for images becomes survival.

chapters.title: Drywall
chapters.summary: Noor cuts open the wall, retrieves twelve years of documents, and burns the rest. A drone passes the window at dusk. Beat: the moment hiding stops being an option and running begins.

chapters.title: Three Flags
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. In three capitals, officials learn Kavanagh may resurface; each government wants the Flight 4471 file closed for different reasons. Introduces the assassin Veyra via contract memo. Beat: machinery of power grinding awake.

chapters.title: Contact
chapters.summary: Noor approaches Mara, half to warn her, half because she's the only thread out. She recognizes him from the crash coverage. Uneasy alliance formed over bad coffee. Beat: two strangers deciding to trust.

chapters.title: Veyra
chapters.summary: Veyra's POV. Methodical, professional, she studies Noor's file and finds it oddly thin — someone has already sanitized it. She begins to wonder who her real employer is. Beat: the hunter develops doubts.

chapters.title: The Rewritten Rules
chapters.summary: Noor decodes anomalies in the official crash report against his evidence: the sensor fault was known before the flight. Reeve calls with new instructions that make no sense. Beat: betrayal sharpening into certainty.

chapters.title: Safe House Two
chapters.summary: A supposed extraction point turns out to be a trap; Noor and Mara escape through storm drains as Veyra arrives seconds late. Beat: terror, then the grim relief of confirmed treachery.

chapters.title: What Mara Saw
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Reviewing her old photo files, she realizes a second person appears in background shots across multiple listings — a courier moving evidence between properties. Beat: the conspiracy widens beyond one house.

chapters.title: Reeve's Confession
chapters.summary: Noor corners Reeve, who admits the program traded silence for contracts years ago but swears he kept Noor's location clean — meaning the leak is higher. Reeve gives him a key. Beat: pity for a compromised man.

chapters.title: The Courier's Flat
chapters.summary: The key opens a flat stacked with duplicates of suppressed findings from other disasters. Noor understands he's one node in a network of bought silence. Beat: private grief becoming public outrage.

chapters.title: Close Quarters
chapters.summary: Veyra catches up in a train station; instead of killing Noor, she asks him one question about her contract's origin. He shows her the sanitized file — her own employers redacted her. Beat: hunter and prey hesitating.

chapters.title: Love Against Duty
chapters.summary: Quiet interlude, alternating POV. In a rented cottage, Noor and Mara stop running for one day. He says his family's names aloud for the first time in years. Beat: tenderness that makes the stakes human.

chapters.title: The Third Government
chapters.summary: They reach a journalist with tribunal connections, but the meeting is leaked; soldiers arrive wearing no flag. Mara is taken. Beat: despair and fury fusing into resolve.

chapters.title: Terms
chapters.summary: Noor offers Veyra the full evidence network in exchange for Mara and passage to the tribunal. Veyra, knowing her employers will erase her too, agrees — conditionally. Beat: enemy becoming reluctant ally.

chapters.title: Exchange
chapters.summary: The handoff goes wrong; Reeve, sent to clean up, dies shielding Noor, whispering which ministry signed the order. Mara is recovered. Beat: sacrifice and momentum.

chapters.title: Siege at the Archive
chapters.summary: Climax part one. Noor, Mara, and Veyra break into the records facility holding the original Flight 4471 black box data while contractors burn files. Beat: race against erasure itself.

chapters.title: Row Twelve, Aloud
chapters.summary: Climax part two. At the emergency hearing, Noor testifies, naming every passenger in row twelve as the room tries to gavel him down. Veyra corroborates with her contract chain. Beat: catharsis — voice versus power.

chapters.title: Aftermath
chapters.summary: Indictments ripple through three governments; the protection program is dissolved. Veyra disappears into negotiation for immunity. Beat: justice partial but real.

chapters.title: Unlisted
chapters.summary: Epilogue, Noor's POV. He and Mara settle somewhere new, unphotographed, unlisted. He plants a garden in rows — twelve of them, though he never explains why. Beat: peace earned, identity chosen rather than assigned.
